newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures open higher with firm dollar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures open higher with firm dollar.

text.p: U.S. debt futures opened higher Friday after finding good support at the overnight low of 111-02 as the dollar rebounded overnight.

The dollar firmed after mixed Japanese economic data diminished expectations for an interest rate hike in that country. The dollar rose one yen overnight and was maintaining gains above 114.00 yen this morning.
Bond floor traders said they suspected hedge funds were buyers in futures on today's open, with a smattering of brokerage houses making purchases of 1,000 lots or more.
Bond traders said technical factors could again dominate activity as they have for the past two sessions, and movement of the stock market could also dictate direction for bonds.

While the September bond contract this week violated some key support levels from the 2 1/2-month uptrend and has posted a series of lower lows, there was good buying interest at the overnight low of 111-02, one brokerage trader said.
He predicted the level would stick as support this session, noting an absence of additional key levels below the market until 110-15, the one-third retracement of the recent rally.

Traders said the market could range trade within narrow parameters, with resistance seen at 111-16, just above the high, seen hemming in prices on the upside. Some quarter-end book-squaring is expected.
This morning, the final revision of first-quarter U.S. gross domestic product was adjusted up slightly to 5.9 percent from the previous estimate of 5.8 percent.
Next week's economic data loom large. First up, May personal income and consumption data, the Chicago Purchasing Management's June survey and May new home sales all will be released on Monday.
